title: Ensemble machine learning identified CDK8 inhibitor hits
summary: A six-model ensemble classified 1.6 million commercial molecules and reduced them to a 1,672-compound CDK8-focused screening library. Docking and visual inspection selected 25 candidates for enzymatic assays; six showed CDK8 inhibition. The most potent hit, T479-0984, had a reported IC50 of 99.9 nM. The paper reports low structural similarity (Tanimoto <0.300) to a comparison set of 30 diverse known CDK8 inhibitors. These are assay hits and starting points, not validated drugs or evidence of therapeutic efficacy.
ai_technology: Six-model ensemble classifier (logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors, support vector classification, random forest, XGBoost and multilayer perceptron)
organization: Taipei Medical University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Shenzhen); Academia Sinica; National Institutes of Health; National Taiwan University

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full text, article metadata, methods/results, author affiliations and compound-level structural comparison reviewed.

evidence.tested: Twenty-five candidates from the focused library underwent CDK8 enzymatic testing; six showed inhibition. T479-0984 was reported with IC50 99.9 nM. The paper compared hits against 30 diverse known CDK8 inhibitors and reports Tanimoto similarity below 0.300.
evidence.unknown: The assay establishes in-vitro enzyme inhibition only, not cellular target engagement, animal efficacy, clinical utility, or exhaustive prior patent/publication status for the compounds.
evidence.ai_role: The six-model ensemble filtered a 1.6-million-molecule commercial library into a 1,672-molecule CDK8-focused library; docking and visual inspection selected candidates that were then tested enzymatically.
